text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit reassures Turks in northern Cyprus of Turkey's permanent support for the breakaway state during his visit to the island to mark the 23rd anniversary of the Turkish invasion.
- Turkish government troops killed 63 rebel Kurds in a two-days of operations in the southeastern Hakkari province.
- Military chiefs deny they are disbanding a unit formed to monitor Islamist activism, saying the fundamentalist threat continues.
- The cabinet of ministers will debate measures to introduce compulsory eight-year education at its Monday meeting.
- Cola Cola will invest $400 million in Turkey in the nexy few years.
- The new goverment will replace around 30 regional governors.
- The private Izmir Cakabey high school is to float shares on the stock exchange, the first schoool in Turkey to do so.
- A group of secularist organisations calls for schools owned by religious foundations to be taken over by the state.
- Sales in ready-wear products have dropped in May and April.
- The village-guards system has spread to the northern province of Ordu as "terrorist" action also widens.
